ui.desc_changelog: Every release of {brand}, with what changed in it.
ui.desc_install: How to install {brand}: distribution packages, building from source, and checksums for every release.
ui.desc_roadmap: What the maintainers of {brand} are working on and what comes next.
ui.nf_text: This page does not exist, or it has moved since the last release.
ui.changelog_intro: Every release, newest first. Version numbers follow the usual major, minor, patch scheme.
ui.install_intro: {brand} is not shipped as a ready-made binary. Distributions package it, and building it from the source archive takes a few minutes.
ui.pkg_note: Package versions can trail the latest release by a few weeks; the table further down says which version to expect from the source archive.
ui.src_intro: You need a C compiler and make. The build takes about a minute. The source archive of each release is named after the version.
ui.sums_intro: Every release has a source archive. Check its SHA-256 checksum before you build it.
ui.roadmap_intro: What the maintainers are working on, in rough order. Plans change; the changelog is the record of what actually happened.
ui.licence_p: {brand} is free software, released under the MIT licence. Use it, change it and share it.

watch.tagline: Run a command when your files change
watch.desc: {brand} watches a folder and runs a command whenever something in it changes.
watch.overview: {brand} watches a folder and runs a command whenever something in it changes. It is a small, fast program for people who are tired of saving a file and then switching to another window.

features.p: One command and no configuration file.
Ignores editor swap files, version control folders and build output.
Linux, macOS and Windows, with the same flags.

changes.t: Support for watching several folders at once.
A delay option to wait for a quiet moment before running.
Colour in the output when the terminal supports it.
A rare crash when a watched folder was deleted.
Duplicate runs when an editor saved a file in two steps.
Paths with spaces on Windows.
The default delay is now 200 milliseconds instead of 50.
Ignore patterns follow the same rules as most version control tools.
A once flag that runs the command a single time and exits.
Memory use growing slowly when watching very large folders.
Error messages now say which folder caused them.
Shell completions for the common shells.

now: Better messages when a command fails
next: A configuration file for per-project settings
Packages for the main Linux distributions
later: A quiet mode for use in scripts

images.tagline: Resize a folder of pictures in one go
images.desc: {brand} resizes and compresses pictures in bulk and leaves the originals alone.
images.overview: {brand} resizes and compresses pictures in bulk. Point it at a folder and say how big you want the results; it does the rest and leaves the originals alone.

features.p: Hundreds of files at once, using every core.
Results go to a new folder.
The same input always gives the same bytes.

changes.t: Support for WebP output.
A quality option for JPEG and WebP.
Photos taken in portrait mode coming out sideways.
A crash on files with no extension.
Output files keep the original modification time.
A dry-run flag that lists what would be done.
Slow progress reporting on large batches.
Smaller memory use when resizing very large pictures.
Resizing to a maximum height as well as a width.
Wrong colours on pictures with an embedded profile.
The help text now has examples.
A suffix option to name the resized files.

now: A progress bar that stays out of the way
next: Packages for the main Linux distributions

markdown.tagline: Catch small mistakes in Markdown before readers do
markdown.desc: {brand} checks Markdown files for broken links, skipped headings and other small mistakes.
markdown.overview: {brand} checks Markdown files for broken links, skipped heading levels, trailing spaces and the other small things that make a document look careless. It runs in a second on a whole documentation folder.

features.p: A thousand files in about a second.
Reports only what it is sure about.
Switch any rule off, or make it stricter.

changes.t: A rule for headings that skip a level.
A rule for links that point to missing files.
False reports for links with anchors.
A crash on files with a byte order mark.
Reports are now sorted by file and line.
An option to fix simple problems automatically.
Rule names are shorter and easier to type.
Wrong line numbers after front matter.
Output as JSON for use in other tools.
Slow checking of very long lines.
The configuration file can now live in any parent folder.
A rule for repeated words.

next: Checking links to headings in other documents
A plugin interface for custom rules

backup.tagline: Plain, dependable backups of a folder
backup.desc: {brand} copies a folder to another place and keeps older versions as ordinary files.
backup.overview: {brand} copies a folder to another place and keeps older versions, so that a mistake last Tuesday can still be undone. Backups are ordinary files that you can open without {brand}.

features.p: No special format to unlock later.
Keep as many snapshots as you like.
A verify command compares a backup with its source.

changes.t: A verify command that compares a backup with its source.
Snapshots can be kept for a number of days or a number of copies.
Files changed during a backup being copied twice.
Wrong permissions on restored files.
Unchanged files are no longer copied again.
A restore command with a dry-run mode.
A crash on folders with very long path names.
Progress is shown only when the output is a terminal.
A list command that shows the snapshots of a backup.
Backups to network drives stopping after a timeout.
Snapshots are named by date rather than by number.
An option to leave out files by pattern.

now: Faster copying of many small files
next: Backing up to a second location in one step
